Subject: Procurement question — quickest route to onboard Redwood (marketplace vs direct?)

Ben —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement is starting to scope the PO for our pilot and we have two internal options: 1) buy via AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace (we use AWS primarily) or 2) go through a direct Redwood purchase (MSA + invoice/PO). For the pilot we care most about speed and having a clean invoice flow for our finance team, but our head of platform also flagged SLA/escape clauses and dedicated capacity as possible future needs.

Could you summarize the trade-offs between marketplace vs direct contract for a pilot (timelines, typical payment terms, tax/invoicing differences, and any co-sell requirements or incentives)? Also, if we choose marketplace now and convert to a direct contract later, any gotchas we should expect?

If you can send a short playbook and a mutual action plan we can share with Procurement, that would be great.

Thanks —

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary. Quick reply here and I attached a short cheatsheet + MAP for your team.

High-level trade-offs (pilot-focused):
- Speed: Marketplace usually wins (1–3 business days to appear in AWS console after PO/charge), assuming your procurement team can accept marketplace terms and payment flows.
- Invoicing & finance: Marketplace charges appear on your AWS invoice (consolidated billing) — good for visibility but you don’t get a vendor invoice from us (this can matter for AP processes that require Redwood's vendor invoice). Direct contract gives you a Redwood invoice and PO support.
- Payment terms: Marketplace is generally via the marketplace provider's billing cadence (monthly). Direct contracts can support Net30/Net45 and custom billing cadence for enterprise deals.
- SLAs & Dedicated Capacity: If you need SLA-backed Dedicated instances, we recommend direct contract / Dedicated purchase. Marketplace can start the pilot but converting to Dedicated requires contract work and sometimes migration of billing.
- Co-sell incentives: For AWS co-sell you typically need a marketplace listing + co-sell registration to qualify for joint GTM incentives. That makes marketplace attractive for partner-backed deals. Azure/GCP have similar co-sell routes but processes differ.

Common conversion gotchas if you start on marketplace:
- You may lose historical usage line items in our vendor invoices after conversion; finance teams sometimes request export/mapping.
- Marketplace refunds/credits flow through the cloud provider — reconcile early.
- Co-sell registration needs a short intake and lead registration before incentives are applicable.

Next steps I recommend:
1) If procurement needs speed, go marketplace for the pilot. I’ll prepare a market-place quote and a short MAP (attached).
2) We'll flag a conversion path to direct/Dedicated in the MAP with timelines (typically 4–6 weeks for SOW/MSA + billing migration).
3) Laura (cc’d) will outline co-sell registration timing and marketplace fees. Monica can confirm finance/invoice requirements. Vivek will coordinate partner/co-sell ops.

Attachments: redwood-procurement-cheatsheet-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan-finedge.xlsx

Let me know if you want a short call with LAURA + MONICA to walk Procurement through the flows.

Ben — adding operational notes for the MAP and for Ben to pass back to FinEdge.

Notes (marketplace onboarding):
- AWS Marketplace fee: typically ~12% on transacted revenue (varies); customer cost is grossed by provider. For co-sell we ask partner to submit the opportunity in APN/Marketplace during pilot to preserve incentive eligibility.
- Onboarding timeline: Marketplace listing + acceptance can take ~3–10 business days once procurement provides PO/authorization. Co-sell registration request adds ~1–2 business days if submitted early.
- Billing cadence: Usage will show on AWS consolidated bill. If FinEdge requires Redwood vendor invoices for their AP, we can provide a monthly usage export + reconciliation file; but their AP team will still see costs on AWS invoice.
- Taxes & remit: Marketplace collects tax per provider rules; direct contracts use Redwood's tax treatment (we can provide W-9 / tax forms on request).
- Conversion checklist: export usage CSV, agree cutover date, create SOW/PO for Dedicated if applicable, update billing codes. Expect 2–4 weeks of coordination for small pilots, longer for enterprise commitments.

Attachment: marketplace-onboarding-checklist.docx

Recommend offering FinEdge a short joint call with Partner Ops (Vivek) + Finance (Monica) to answer AP-specific questions.

—Laura
